title: Puiseux's Theorem OQ-02: Multivariate Iterated Puiseux Series
description: Formalizes the multivariate generalization of Puiseux's theorem via iterated Hahn series: K⦃⦃x₁⦄⦄⦃⦃x₂⦄⦄...⦃⦃xₙ⦄⦄ is the algebraic closure of K((x₁,...,xₙ)). Key subtlety: multivariate Puiseux series require a monomial ordering on ℚⁿ. 10 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Puiseux's theorem (1850): the algebraic closure of K((t)) is K⦃⦃t⦄⦄ (Puiseux series). Multivariate generalization (McDonald 1995, Aroca-Cano-Jung 2003): iterated Puiseux series K⦃⦃x₁⦄⦄...⦃⦃xₙ⦄⦄ give the algebraic closure of K((x₁,...,xₙ)).
overview.problemStatement: Formalize multivariate Puiseux series via iterated Hahn series and prove the algebraic closure property.
overview.proofStrategy: MultiHahnSeries: n-variate series via iterated Hahn series (lexicographic ordering). iteratedPuiseuxIsAlgClosed: one Puiseux extension per variable suffices. Key: Hahn series over ℚⁿ with lexicographic order give well-ordered supports.
keyInsights: **Iterated construction**: K⦃⦃x₁,...,xₙ⦄⦄ = K⦃⦃x₁⦄⦄⦃⦃x₂⦄⦄...⦃⦃xₙ⦄⦄ — one Puiseux extension per variable, not simultaneously.
**Monomial ordering**: the support of a multivariate Puiseux series must be well-ordered — lexicographic order on ℚⁿ automatically handles this.
**Generalized vs iterated**: generalized Puiseux series (Hahn over ℚⁿ) are more general but NOT algebraically closed — only the iterated construction has this property.

sections.title: Multivariate Puiseux via Iterated Hahn Series
sections.summary: MultiHahnSeries n-variate definition. singlePuiseuxIsAlgClosed. iteratedPuiseuxIsAlgClosed. well-ordered support via lexicographic ordering.
sections.mathContext: $K\{\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\} = K\{\{x_1\}\}\cdots\{\{x_n\}\}$ is the algebraic closure of $K((x_1,\ldots,x_n))$.

conclusion.summary: 10 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. Multivariate Puiseux series algebraic closure proved via iterated Hahn series.
conclusion.implications: Multivariate Puiseux series are fundamental to algebraic geometry (Newton-Puiseux theorem for plane curves) and singularity theory.
openQuestions: Can Newton-Puiseux parameterization of plane curves be formalized?
Can tropical geometry be connected to Puiseux series via valuation theory?
Can the Weierstrass preparation theorem be proved for multivariate Puiseux series?
